https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cj06.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Vessels were visible across the Strait of Hormuz from Oman this week By Joe Coughlan Published 1 September 2026 Updated 2 hours ago American forces resumed strikes against Iran on Tuesday, US Central Command (Centcom) has said. Centcom said the US strikes followed "recent attempted attacks" by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian Red Crescent said four people including a young child were killed in the US attacks, and more than 50 injured, when after a US missile attack shrapnel hit a home where a wedding celebration was taking place in Sirik in southern Iran. In response, Iran launched attacks at US military bases in Iraq and Jordan, according to local state media and the Jordanian Armed Forces. Attacks were also reported in Kuwait and Bahrain. The IRGC said the US would "regret" the strikes. By early Wednesday, it had launched a barrage of ballistic missiles at a US Marine base in Jordan's Aqaba in retaliation for the Sirik attack, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency. The Jordanian Armed Forces said it had intercepted 13 ballistic missiles, 10 of which were destroyed, while three fell in remote areas. There were no deaths or injuries as a result of the attack from Iran. The network also said that the country's national security centre had warned residents of the Aqaba and Mafraq governates of falling debris, adding that the warning had since ended. Separately, the Kuwait army said its air defences were responding to Iranian missile attacks early Wednesday. Several explosions were also reported in Bahrain following attacks by Iran, according to Iranian state media. Donald Trump, when the US strikes were announced on Tuesday afternoon, warned that Iran would be hit again at "a much harder and higher level" if it retaliated. The attack follows the first known US strikes on Iran since late July earlier this week, when forces attacked two rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait. Tehran retaliated by firing missiles at air bases in Jordan and a drone at the UAE. Centcom said US forces had begun striking IRGC targets at 12:00 ET (16:00 GMT), and had completed the strikes by early Wednesday. Iranian state media reported a four-year-old child was among the four who had died in the Sirik attack, while other reports said projectiles had hit the areas of Chabahar and Konarak and an airport in Jiroft, and that explosions were heard in Qeshm island and Bandar Abbas. US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins, speaking on behalf of Centcom, told the BBC it was aware of reports from Iranian state media of the attack in Sirik. He added: "The US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC." The US and Israel launched wide-ranging strikes on Iran on 28 February, with Iran responding by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to marine traffic. A US-Iran agreement, known as the Memorandum of Understanding, to extend a ceasefire between the two countries was signed in June. However that agreement has expired, leading to a resumption of hostilities. Both the US and Iran have also fired on shipping, with Tehran targeting vessels it says have sought to cross the Strait without its permission and the US enforcing a naval blockade of Iranian ports. Washington also announced a fresh sanctions campaign on 24 August aimed at further isolating Tehran and expanding secondary sanctions against its allies. Speaking at a G20 finance ministers meeting, the US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that many US allies "came forward and said they will do whatever is necessary" concerning the sanctions against Iran. Iranian officials and state media have largely dismissed the campaign as a continuation of previous US economic measures, which they argue followed Washington's military failure in the recent conflict. However on Tuesday Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian was quoted by state media as saying if the US returned to committing to the agreement, Iran would reciprocate. Two Men Detained After Allegedly Assaulting Police Officer During Bar Disturbance in Eastern Romania Deșteptarea 30 august 2026 se citește în 1 min. Acțiune Facebook X WhatsApp Telegram VK Two men, aged 51 and 27, have been detained for 24 hours after allegedly assaulting a police officer responding to a disturbance at a bar in Faraoani commune, Bacău County, police said. According to the Bacău County Police Inspectorate, the incident occurred on the evening of Aug. 29, at around 8:30 p.m., after a bar employee called the national emergency number 112 to report that several customers were behaving aggressively inside the premises. A patrol from the Rural Police Section in Răcăciuni was dispatched to the scene. While officers were identifying those involved, two of the men allegedly refused to comply with police instructions and attacked the officers. After one of the officers was struck by one of the suspects, his colleague fired warning shots into the air using his service weapon. The two men then fled the scene, police said. A joint investigative team subsequently identified and located the suspects, aged 51 and 27. Based on the evidence gathered, the case prosecutor ordered their detention for 24 hours. Both men were taken to the detention and pre-trial arrest facility operated by the Bacău County Police Inspectorate. The investigation is being conducted by the Prosecutor’s Office attached to the Bacău District Court. The suspects are being investigated on allegations of assaulting a police officer, making threats, and disturbing public order. https://avweb.com/aviation-news/avionics.text: The former owner of a Kansas avionics company has been sentenced to 18 months in federal prison for his involvement in a scheme to illegally export aviation technology to Russia. According to the Justice Department , Cyril Gregory Buyanovsky, 63, of Lawrence, Kansas, pleaded guilty to conspiracy and money laundering related to the sale of controlled avionics equipment without the required export licenses. Buyanovsky was formerly president of KanRus Trading Company, which continued supplying Russian customers after the United States tightened export restrictions following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine beginning in 2022. Federal prosecutors said the company concealed the intended recipients of its shipments and used intermediaries in other countries to circumvent export controls. Yearslong Export Scheme According to an earlier DOJ announcement , Buyanovsky admitted that he, along with associates, exported a repaired TCAS to the Russian Federal Security Service in 2021. Conspirators removed identifying markings before having the equipment repaired by a U.S. company. Once repairs were made, the equipment was returned to Russia. According to investigation findings, the group also utilized false export documentation, along with routing payments through foreign bank accounts. Three Defendants Sentenced “The defendants ignored those laws and saw the war not as a humanitarian crisis, but as a business opportunity to boost their profits,” U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser said in the September sentencing announcement. Buyanovsky agreed to forfeit more than $450,000 in avionics equipment and accessories, along with a $50,000 personal forfeiture judgment. His sentencing follows the convictions of two associates. Former KanRus Vice President Douglas Robertson received a 32-month prison sentence in June, while Latvian broker Oleg Chistyakov was sentenced to 28 months. The FBI and Department of Commerce’s Office of Export Enforcement investigated the case, assisted by Latvian authorities and U.S. Customs and Border Protection. https://hotnews.ro/anxietate-de-la-kiev-.text: Întâlnirea preconizată între cei mai puternici trei lideri ai lumii generează anxietate de la Kiev până la Tokyo, potrivit unor persoane informate despre reacțiile acestor guverne, a scris Reuters într-o analiză înaintea summitului dintre președinții Statelor Unite, Chinei și Rusiei. Casa Albă a confirmat oficial că președintele american Donald Trump se va întâlni cu omologii săi din Rusia și China , joia viitoare, în marja reuniunii Cooperării Economice Asia-Pacific (APEC) de la Shenzhen. Summitul planificat a fost comparat cu Conferința de la Yalta din 1945, mai ales în Rusia. Întâlnirea pe care au avut-o liderii de atunci ai Statelor Unite, Regatului Unit și Uniunii Sovietice în urmă cu 81 de ani în Crimeea a formalizat sferele de influență și a pregătit terenul pentru ordinea postbelică, devenind un simbol al înțelegerilor dintre marile puteri impuse țărilor mici, explică Reuters . În această săptămână, ideologul naționalist rus Aleksandr Dughin a declarat pentru Radio Sputnik că summitul „este profund simbolic” și reprezintă „o confirmare a unei lumi multipolare pe care Occidentul o neagă”. Pentru naționaliștii ruși, perspectiva unui eveniment de tip Yalta generează entuziasm, în condițiile în care ar putea deschide calea spre un acord pentru de încheiere a războiului din Ucraina într-un mod care ar favoriza Moscova. Totuși, pentru guvernele unor țări mai mici, ca Ucraina sau Taiwan, posibilitatea unor înțelegeri de culise între SUA, Rusia și China reprezintă un motiv de profundă neliniște. „Chiar nu vrem ca asta să se transforme în «Yalta 2, 3, 4», cu o redistribuire a influenței”, spunea luna trecută președintele ucrainean Volodimir Zelenski. Deși perspectivele pentru concretizarea unui acord major sunt considerate a fi mici, cei trei lideri vin la summit cu obiective foarte diferite, iar întâlnirea le oferă ocazia de a discuta puncte fierbinți de pe agenda globală, de la războaiele din Ucraina și Iran până la armele nucleare și inteligența artificială. Președintele rus Vladimir Putin are șansa de a obține un acord pentru soluționarea conflictului din Ucraina în termenii săi. Trump, al cărui Partid Republican a suferit în această lună o înfrângere grea la alegerile intermediare din SUA, ar putea căuta succese pe plan extern și vede un moment demn de cărțile de istorie, cu posibile progrese spre un acord în trei privind controlul armelor nucleare. În schimb, pentru liderul chinez Xi Jinping, este o reuniune imprevizibilă, plină de riscuri. Rusia și Statele Unite dețin peste 5.000 de focoase nucleare fiecare, în timp ce China are în jur de 500. Deși își extinde rapid arsenalul, Beijingul se simte dezavantajat pe plan nuclear. „Este ceva ce chinezii urăsc”, a spus Edgard Kagan, fost înalt oficial pentru Asia de Est la Casa Albă în timpul administrației Biden, care lucrează acum la think-tank-ul Center for Strategic and International Studies. În opinia expertului, Beijingul nu își dorește discuții despre controlul armelor în acest moment – și cu atât mai puțin cu SUA și Rusia, „pentru că asta ar sugera că acceptă încadrarea potrivit căreia sunt acum o mare putere nucleară care ar trebui să fie supusă unor restricții similare”. Cercetători chinezi intervievați de Reuters au declarat, la rândul lor, că sugestia lui Trump privind discuții nucleare este exclusă din start pentru Beijing. „Nu ne așteptăm să ajungem la vreun fel de acord” pe teme nucleare, a declarat un înalt oficial al administrației Trump, adăugând, însă, că „este timpul” ca Beijingul să abordeze acest subiect. Deși Rusia și China s-au apropiat în ultimii ani, au abordări diferite față de summit. Moscova și-a dorit o discuție despre războiul din Ucraina, însă Beijingul s-a împotrivit includerii acestui subiect pe agendă, au spus una dintre persoanele informate despre întâlnire și un diplomat european, sub condiția anonimatului. Vineri, un oficial american a afirmat că este puțin probabil ca Trump să aducă în discuție războiul din Ucraina și că un astfel de summit nu reprezintă formatul adecvat pentru asta. Photograph: Stuart Boulton/Alamy Schools Schools in England must set aside time for pupils to read for pleasure Education secretary expected to announce measures as part of proposed reforms to national curriculum Nadeem Badshah Fri 27 Nov 2026 18.34 EST Last modified on Fri 27 Nov 2026 18.45 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Schools in England will have to allocate time for children to read for pleasure as part of Labour’s proposed reforms of the national curriculum. The education secretary, Lucy Powell , is expected to announce to parliament on Monday that primary schools must earmark time each day for children to read. High screen time can hurt children’s learning and language skills, study suggests Read more Secondary schools will be required to set aside time several days a week as part of the measures to tackle declining literacy rates and increasing screen time. There will be a statutory reading test for children in year 8, and secondary schools will be expected to ensure pupils focus on entire books, poems and other literature. The education secretary told the Times: “Across the world, we are seeing a ticking timebomb for our future generations as reading and literacy levels are falling, with too many children seeing reading as a chore or missing out altogether. “We cannot afford to stand idly by and let this continue. Reading fluently is the gateway to lifelong learning, opening up every subject in school.” Powell added that in addition to setting up children for success, reading should be “enjoyed and every child should have the opportunity to discover that”. Powell is also expected to announce the programmes of study for the curriculum in England, which could include shorter exams in some GCSE subjects. History, geography and modern foreign languages are considered the most likely courses to be slimmed down. Laura Trott, the shadow education secretary, said she welcomed reforms that encouraged children to read more but said they “must go hand in hand with a serious effort to reduce screen time in our classrooms”. Only 10% of boys aged 14-16 read daily for pleasure, National Literacy Trust finds Read more In July, an education committee inquiry into reading for pleasure concluded that the National Year of Reading should be extended to a National Decade of Reading . It called on the government to commit to a national reading guarantee that would ensure all children have regular opportunities to enjoy reading. Research last year found that reading enjoyment among children and young people in the UK had fallen to its lowest level in two decades , with a sharper decline among teenage boys. While boys’ reading enjoyment fell across most age groups – particularly among those aged 11 to 16 – for girls it remained relatively stable or slightly improved. The National Literacy Trust’s survey found that among girls aged eight to 18, 39.1% said they enjoyed reading in their free time, compared with 25.7% of boys.
